transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Cascade Head of ML), Tom Alvarez (Cascade Platform Eng), Ethan Brooks (Cascade CTO)

[00:00] Alyssa Chen: hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm alyssa from redwood, quick intro round?
[00:08] Priya Nair: hey alyssa, priya here. we're looking at structured outputs for our customer support routing use case.
[00:12] Tom Alvarez: tom, platform. we care about latency and how this fits into our k8s infra.
[00:15] Ethan Brooks: ethan, cto. high level: we need deterministic json payloads for downstream systems.
[00:25] Alyssa Chen: awesome. Marcus will lead the demo, i'll chime on pricing and next steps.

--- Demo / Walkthrough ---
[02:10] Marcus Li: okay jumping in — goal for today: show JSON mode/structured output, function calling/tool integration, and guardrails the console gives. first slide is a sample schema, simple ticket schema: {"ticket_id":"string","priority":"enum(low,med,high)","category":"string"} — we'll demo both schema validation and recovery behaviors. (note: slide showed link to docs: https://redwood.ai/structured-output)
[03:05] Priya Nair: quick q — do you support optional fields and nested objects? our events have nested metadata.
[03:20] Marcus Li: yes, nested schemas are supported. we also show an example of partial outputs and how the runtime returns error codes and a normalized response so your pipeline can fallback.
[04:00] Tom Alvarez: how deterministic is this? we can't have downstream jobs break because of small variations.
[04:18] Marcus Li: good question — JSON mode plus strict schema enforcement yields high determinism. the runtime runs a post-processor that attempts to coerce close matches, and if it can't, it flags the output as invalid and we can route to a fallback model or queue it for manual review. you can configure strict vs lenient modes in the console or via api param.
[05:40] Ethan Brooks: what about function calling? we want the model to emit a function call to kick off our enrichment service rather than raw JSON.
[05:55] Marcus Li: yep, function/tool calling is supported — both via the API and the Console. we demonstrated mapping model outputs to a tool schema, and the runtime will call the tool agent with the structured payload. we also have tracing in the console so you can see the call chain.
[06:30] Marcus Li: (demo) here's the live api call: model=redwood-structured-1, mode=json, schema=company_ticket_v2. streaming=true, call_function="enrich_ticket". watch the right pane for streaming tokens and the final json.
[07:05] [demo noise, typing]
[07:40] [00:07:40] Marcus Li: okay final payload arrived: {"ticket_id":"T-2345","priority":"high","category":"billing","meta":{"orig_text":"customer says invoice wrong"}}
[08:10] Priya Nair: that looks good. if the model hallucinated a new field, would schema validation drop it?
[08:22] Marcus Li: by default additional properties are stripped, but you can choose to surface them in a separate field for auditing. also our optimize product can suggest quantization/profile changes to lower cost for that workload.

--- Security / Compliance / Private deployment discussion ---
[11:05] Ethan Brooks: we are regulated in EU and want data residency + customer-managed keys. what are our options for private deployment?
[11:19] Alyssa Chen: we have Redwood Private — VPC/on-prem deployment. supports KMS/HSM integrations, SSO/SAML, RBAC. we can also run a private control plane with your network.
[11:45] Tom Alvarez: audit logs — we need immutable logs and retention for 7 years in our audit.
[11:55] Marcus Li: console has audit logs export; for Private deployments we can keep logs in your S3/GCS with lifecycle policies. SOC 2/ISO docs are in the security pack I'll share.
[12:35] Priya Nair: what about e2e encryption of KV cache? our prompts contain PII.
[12:45] Marcus Li: KV cache can be encrypted with your keys. we recommend prefix caching for non-sensitive prefixes; for sensitive data you should use encryption + redaction at ingestion. we'll share the security whitepaper.

--- Integration and Performance ---
[15:20] Tom Alvarez: on throughput — our peak is ~120rps with avg seq length 400 tokens. what throughput can Dedicated provide?
[15:34] Marcus Li: Dedicated pools can hit that easily with batching; exact numbers depend on model and quantization. for a 7b optimized model with q4_0 and batching of 8 we typically see X tokens/sec on an A100-like instance; i'll follow up with a latency/throughput table.
[16:00] Ethan Brooks: any concerns about cold starts? we can't have >300ms p95 in our pipeline.
[16:12] Marcus Li: cold start mitigation via warm pool and autoscaling policies. Dedicated supports pinned capacity and pre-warmed workers. we'd recommend a reserved capacity plan for your SLA.
[17:00] Priya Nair: can we run the live function-calling in our staging env? we don't want the model to call prod tools during tests.
[17:12] Alyssa Chen: yes, you can configure tool endpoints per environment and restrict via RBAC. there's also a sandbox mode so calls are logged but not executed.

--- Guardrails and Observability ---
[20:05] Marcus Li: guardrails: schema enforcement, token-level cost limits, and post-generation validators. Console shows per-route breakdowns; Optimize suggests batching and quantization settings. Also set post-generation checks that reject outputs if they fail entity validation.
[21:10] Tom Alvarez: how does retried requests affect idempotency? if the function call fails mid-way do you dedupe?
[21:26] Marcus Li: we have request ids and function call ids — the runtime supports exactly-once semantics for built-in tool adapters; for custom endpoints we provide an idempotency token in the payload so your service can handle dedupe.

--- Live PoC plan discussion ---
[25:30] Alyssa Chen: recommended PoC: one-week pilot on staging, 1k daily calls with our structured model, run a few reroutes to test fallbacks. success criteria: >=98% valid json + p95 latency <350ms.
[26:05] Priya Nair: timeline — we want this in sept, ideally the week of 9/15.
[26:20] Ethan Brooks: budget — approximate cost?
[26:30] Alyssa Chen: i'll send a ballpark price for hosted vs dedicated. Hosted is usage based; Dedicated is reserved capacity. we'll include estimated cost for your 120rps peak.

--- Questions and objections ---
[29:00] Tom Alvarez: what about model updates? if you update the model weights, will that break our schema?
[29:12] Marcus Li: we support model pinning by version and staged rollouts (canary, A/B). plus we tie evals to prompt sets and monitor regressions; Optimize alerts on quality drift.
[30:20] Priya Nair: curious about fallback routing — do you route to a smaller cheaper model automatically?
[30:30] Marcus Li: yes, smart routing policies can route by latency, cost, or region. you can set automatic fallback to a compatible model variant.

--- Small transcription hiccup / natural speech ---
[33:05] Ethan Brooks: so if the model calls enrich ticket, will that call carry the kv cahce context?
[33:20] Marcus Li: kv cache, yeah, uh kv cache context is maintained per request session but we scrub sensitive fields unless configured otherwise. (laughs) sorry, cache — the transcription had a small glitch.

--- Closing / Recap / Next steps ---
[38:00] Alyssa Chen: recap: 1) we'll send structured output guide and sample schema, 2) security pack (SOC2/ISO + whitepaper), 3) pricing estimate + PoC plan for week of 9/15.
[38:25] Priya Nair: ok good. Marcus will run a pre-PoC benchmark?
[38:30] Marcus Li: yes i'll run a micro-benchmark and share latency sheets.
[38:45] Tom Alvarez: i'll share our staging endpoint and teams contact for tool integration.
[39:00] Ethan Brooks: agreed. one more ask — can you include an example of streaming + recovery on partial jsons?
[39:12] Marcus Li: yes i'll include a demo gif and a transcript of the streaming example.
[40:00] Alyssa Chen: great — we'll follow up with docs and get the PoC scheduled. thanks all.
[40:20] Priya Nair: thanks everyone.
[40:25] Tom Alvarez: thanks.
[40:30] [meeting ends]
